question: What is the main goal of Primary Health Care (PHC)?

options.A: Building specialized tertiary hospitals in every local government
options.B: Bringing essential health care close to where people live
options.C: Training foreign medical doctors for rural service postings
options.D: Providing free medications for chronic non-communicable diseases

explanation: Spot on! PHC is all about bringing basic, necessary health services right to people's doorsteps or communities, so nobody has to travel miles just to see a nurse or doctor. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T3#GNS124_U4_T3_h1)

question: How does community mobilisation change the way local people take part in health programs?

options.A: It makes villagers responsible for hiring and firing doctors
options.B: It forces community members to fund all local clinic budgets
options.C: It turns passive recipients into active partners in health
options.D: It replaces the need for professional nurses in rural areas

explanation: You got it! Instead of just waiting for health workers to tell them what to do, mobilisation gets community members involved as active partners in their own wellbeing. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T3#GNS124_U4_T3_h1)

question: In community health, what does 'self-reliance' actually mean?

options.A: Patients treating their own severe illnesses without nurses
options.B: Villages building their own roads and electricity networks
options.C: Hospitals refusing to accept government grants or donations
options.D: Communities maintaining health improvements after external projects end

explanation: Brilliant! Self-reliance means a community has learned enough and built enough capacity to keep their health programs running smoothly even after the NGO or government project packs up and leaves. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T3#GNS124_U4_T3_h2)

question: Why is it so important to involve the community at every single stage of a health program?

options.A: It completely eliminates the need for baseline surveys
options.B: It allows the government to avoid paying health workers
options.C: It ensures interventions address real, locally felt needs
options.D: It speeds up the construction of primary health centers

explanation: Spot on! When locals help plan from day one, we make sure we are actually solving the problems they care about most, rather than guessing what they need. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T3#GNS124_U4_T3_h2)

question: What is the biggest benefit of working hand-in-hand with local leaders during health campaigns?

options.A: They diagnose complex medical conditions in clinics
options.B: They guarantee immediate funding from international donors
options.C: They help dispel cultural myths and reduce resistance
options.D: They replace the need for public health education entirely

explanation: You're right! Local leaders are trusted voices. When they speak up in favor of a health drive, community members feel much safer and more willing to listen. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T3#GNS124_U4_T3_h3)

question: A village is turning down a new immunization drive because of heavy rumors. What should you do first?

options.A: Ignore the rumors and continue vaccinating those who show up voluntarily
options.B: Engage trusted community leaders and local influencers to discuss concerns
options.C: Report the community to security forces for refusing public health care
options.D: Cancel the immunization program and shift supplies to urban centers

explanation: Exactly! Working through respected local figures is the best way to clear up misunderstandings, answer questions, and build genuine trust. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T3#GNS124_U4_T3_h3)

question: How can rural communities creatively solve the problem of getting sick patients to a clinic?

options.A: Organizing local emergency transport systems like tricycles
options.B: Waiting for ambulances to be stationed in every street
options.C: Demanding that the government buy cars for every family
options.D: Building major federal highways to connect every village

explanation: Spot on! Communities often band together to arrange local transport like branded tricycles or bikes to bridge the gap during emergencies. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T3#GNS124_U4_T3_h4)

question: Why do dialogue groups involving village elders and men help improve women's health access?

options.A: They address cultural norms that restrict women from seeking care
options.B: They replace the professional nursing staff in maternal wards
options.C: They prevent women from leaving their homes for any reason
options.D: They give men exclusive control over clinic budgets and supplies

explanation: You got it! Since elders and men often hold decision-making power in the home, getting them on board helps remove cultural blocks that stop women from getting timely care. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T3#GNS124_U4_T3_h4)

question: As a nurse entering a brand new community, what should always be your very first step?

options.A: Listening to the community before telling them what to do
options.B: Demanding that the village head build a new health post
options.C: Distributing medications without proper medical evaluations
options.D: Issuing strict rules on sanitation and personal hygiene

explanation: Brilliant! Listening first shows respect. It helps you understand their everyday realities and priorities before you try to introduce any changes. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T3#GNS124_U4_T3_h5)

question: Why is it smart to partner with existing groups like age-grades or church/mosque committees?

options.A: They are legally required to manage government health clinics
options.B: They provide a steady source of income for health workers
options.C: They already hold influence and command trust among members
options.D: They possess formal medical training recognized by the ministry

explanation: Spot on! Working through groups that people already belong to and trust makes it much easier to share important health messages. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T3#GNS124_U4_T3_h5)

question: Apart from bedside clinical work, what is a key role for a community health nurse?

options.A: Purchasing medical equipment for tertiary teaching hospitals
options.B: Financing the construction of primary healthcare centers
options.C: Acting as an educator and facilitator for health programs
options.D: Drafting national health policies in the federal ministry

explanation: You nailed it! Community nurses spend a lot of time teaching families, running workshops, and helping communities organize their own health activities. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T3#GNS124_U4_T3_h6)

question: What does 'cultural humility' mean for a nurse working in community health?

options.A: It prevents patients from asking questions about their treatment
options.B: It allows the nurse to bypass standard medical protocols safely
options.C: It ensures the nurse receives financial awards from village chiefs
options.D: It helps the nurse respect local beliefs and build genuine trust

explanation: Spot on! Cultural humility means approaching people with an open, respectful mind, honoring their traditions while gently sharing health knowledge. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T3#GNS124_U4_T3_h6)

question: What is the clearest sign that a community health project has achieved sustainability?

options.A: International donors continue sending large sums of money
options.B: The primary health clinic closes down due to lack of patients
options.C: The local government takes over the salaries of all foreign staff
options.D: The community continues health practices after project staff leave

explanation: You got it! Sustainability means the good habits and programs keep running successfully even after external helpers have packed up and gone home. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T3#GNS124_U4_T3_h7)

question: Why is it important to share evaluation results back with the community members?

options.A: It proves to them that health workers are superior planners
options.B: It eliminates the need for any future community meetings
options.C: It forces them to pay taxes for the healthcare they received
options.D: It maintains motivation and highlights areas for improvement

explanation: Brilliant! Giving feedback lets the community see the impact of their hard work, keeps them excited, and guides what needs fixing next. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T3#GNS124_U4_T3_h7)
